function: MA-PPO agents jointly choose BS precoders, common-stream rate, RIS phase shifts and uplink powers to maximize full-duplex RSMA sum rate under imperfect CSI (pp. 6, 8).
system: Full-duplex BS with 4 transmit and 4 receive antennas, RSMA, 4 downlink and 4 uplink single-antenna vehicles, reflecting RIS with 64 elements, 24.2 GHz carrier (pp. 3, 11).
method: Multi-agent PPO with downlink and uplink agents, actor-critic networks of two hidden layers (256 neurons), reinforcement learning with a memory buffer, 2000 episodes (pp. 7-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician fading with LoS array responses and Rayleigh NLoS, norm-bounded CSI errors, power-law path loss (exponent 3.5 and 2.8); no dataset or measurements (pp. 5, 10).
test_conditions: Default K=U=4, N=64, 30 m/s (p. 11); sum rate plotted versus vehicles, RIS elements, antennas, speed and power; no separate test set or adaptation described (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Classical: none. Learned: single-agent PPO and DDPG, each also in half-duplex mode; SDMA and perfect-CSI variants of the same DRL schemes (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Sum rate in bits/s/Hz (total, downlink and uplink), reward per episode, episodes to convergence (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Table II gives O(.) expressions for MA-PPO, PPO and DDPG in the RIS size N, samples l_a, buffer W and epsilon; no runtime or parameter count (p. 11).
openness: none; no link to code or data.
q1_support: p. 5: "we use the Rician distribution to represent each of the DL channels"; NLoS parts are Rayleigh and path loss is a power law (p. 10), so the channel is a custom simulator with no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing set or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "Unless stated otherwise, the parameter settings adhere to the aforementioned specifications."; Figs. 4-7 and 9 plot sum rate versus vehicles, RIS elements, antennas and speed, but no passage says a trained policy is tested on unseen settings or adapted.
q3_support: p. 12: "we conduct a comparison between the proposed FD system and its HD counterpart for the benchmark PPO and DDPG schemes"; PPO and DDPG are learned, and HD and SDMA are also solved with DRL (Fig. 7 labels MA-PPO-SDMA), so no non-learned method (random or fixed RIS, optimization) is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "we address the computational complexity of the MA-PPO-based algorithm, as well as the PPO and DDPG algorithms, as depicted in Table II"; Table II (p. 11) lists the O(.) expressions.
q5_support: p. 5: "we use the Rician distribution to represent each of the DL channels"; channels are simulated, and the paper gives no link, DOI or public dataset for code or data.
notes: Area 3: the learned MA-PPO sets the BS precoders, RIS phase shifts and powers (action space, p. 8). q1: Rician and Rayleigh fading with a power-law path loss, no 3GPP model. q2: the sweeps over vehicles, RIS elements, antennas and speed are not described as tests of a trained model in new conditions; the action space depends on N and the number of vehicles, so each point probably needs its own training, but the paper does not say. q3: only learned baselines (PPO, DDPG) are compared; the HD, SDMA and perfect-CSI variants are run with DRL as well. q4: Table II gives complexity orders, not runtimes. The action space also lists channel error vectors (p. 8), which does not change the area.
